chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A believer's light shines for the inhabitants of the heavens like stars shining for the inhabitants of the earth.
He also said: A believer is a friend of Allah; he helps Him and works for Him and he does not say concerning Allah anything but the truth; and he does not fear anyone other than Him.
He also said: When two believers meet and shake hands, Allah does not cease looking at them and their sins continue to fall off them until they part.

key_terms.مُقْبِلًا بِوَجْهِهِ: facing them with His face (divine attention)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of a believer's light and interaction with God?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this hadith from *Kitab al-Mumin* elucidates the metaphysical reality of the believer's *nur* (light), illustrating how spiritual purity renders the faithful visible to the celestial realm. It emphasizes the believer's status as *wali Allah*, characterized by truthfulness and fearlessness, while describing the mutual greeting (*tasaful*) between believers as a moment of divine favor where sins are shed like dust, reflecting the concept of *tawassul* through righteous companionship.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 54. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:
A believer's light shines for the inhabitants of the heavens like stars shining for the inhabitants of the earth.
He also said: A believer is a friend of Allah; he helps Him and works for Him and he does not say concerning Allah anything but the truth; and he does not fear anyone other than Him.
He also said: When two believers meet and shake hands, Allah does not cease looking at them and their sins continue to fall off them until they part.
